data.title: Giancarlo Links $6 Billion Crypto Hack to Firm Security, Backs Federal CFTC Oversight
data.description:
The $6 billion crypto hack has renewed debate over digital-asset security and regulation, Bloomberg reported. Former CFTC Chairman J. Christopher Giancarlo said the attack exposed vulnerabilities at an individual firm, not a failure of underlying blockchain technology.

Giancarlo called for the US to take a more aggressive approach to state-sponsored cyberattacks and said prediction markets should be regulated federally by the CFTC rather than by individual states.

data.title: Fitch Moves France's Rating Outlook to Negative Amid Budget Strains
data.description: Fitch Ratings placed France's credit rating on a negative outlook in an unscheduled move, according to Bloomberg, as the country struggles to fix its public finances.

data.title: Alphabet (GOOG.O) in Talks to Join $185 Billion Golden Dome Program
data.description: According to Jin10, Alphabet (GOOG.O), Google's parent company, is in talks with the Pentagon about joining U.S. President Donald Trump's $185 billion Golden Dome missile-defense program. Alphabet would focus on data security, storage, networking and cybersecurity capabilities to help protect data transmissions for military command-and-control software from attacks. The discussions are at an early stage, and Google's networking company Aalyria is also involved in preparations for a related coalition. The Pentagon said it has not made a final decision on forming a new coalition or which companies would participate.

data.title: PacSun CEO Says Brands Matter to Young Consumers
data.description:
PacSun CEO Brieane Olson said brands mean a lot to young people today. The retailer’s core customer is 16 to 24, and it tracks differences between Gen Z and Gen Alpha, Bloomberg reported.

A PacSun Youth Report conducted with GlobalData and surveying 6,000 young people found mental health was their top priority, Olson said. She cited PacSun’s ongoing partnership with Selena Gomez and the Rare Impact Foundation as a collaboration intended to have lasting value for young customers. Olson spoke with Romaine Bostick on “The Close” on October 29, 2026.

data.title: predict.fun Puts HLE at 79% to Beat G2 in LoL S16 Swiss Match, With Loser Eliminated
data.description:
predict.fun lists HLE’s probability of beating G2 in the League of Legends S16 Swiss stage at 79%. According to Odaily, the teams are scheduled to play a best-of-three match at about 6:30 a.m. today, with both entering at 1-2. The winner will move to the 2-2 group and continue competing for a quarterfinal spot, while the loser will be eliminated at 1-3.

G2 lost its opening match to LCK team DK, beat Pacific region team TSW, then lost to LPL team TES. HLE opened with a win over TES, then lost to GEN and IG.

data.title: Chainlink Reserve Adds 427,600 LINK in October, Total Holdings Reach 6.4751 Million
data.description: Chainlink Reserve added 427,600 LINK in October, spending more than $5.3 million and bringing its total holdings to 6.4751 million LINK. According to Odaily, Chainlink said the reserve is intended to support the network’s long-term growth and sustainability.

data.title: Opay Shares Remain Untraded After $304 Million US IPO
data.description: Opay Ltd., a Nigeria-focused payments platform, raised $304 million in a US initial public offering priced at the bottom of the range, but its shares did not begin trading in New York as expected, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Ice Cube Says Big3 Is Positioned to Scale
data.description: Ice Cube, CEO and co-founder of the Big3 basketball league, said audiences want more basketball in the summer and that the league has helped professionalize three-on-three play. He called basketball globally beloved and said Big3 is well positioned to grow, describing it as the world’s premier professional three-on-three league, Bloomberg reported. He spoke with Romaine Bostick on “The Close” on October 29, 2026.

data.title: New Balance CEO Joe Preston: NYC Marathon Partnership Is Key to Brand
data.description: New Balance President and CEO Joe Preston described the company’s long-running partnership with the New York City Marathon as a key part of the brand, according to Bloomberg. More than 300 New Balance associates are in the city for race week, including 200 retail staff at the Javits Center expo, where more than 100,000 visitors are expected over three days. Preston spoke with Romaine Bostick on “The Close” on October 29, 2026.

data.title: UKMTO Reports Two Vessel Attack Incidents
data.description: On October 30, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported two vessel attack incidents. According to Sina Finance, one vessel was struck by an unidentified projectile on its port side about 40 nautical miles south of Iran’s Lavan Island and caught fire; its crew was confirmed safe, and no environmental pollution was reported. UKMTO also received a delayed report, based on verified sources, that a tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile while leaving the Strait of Hormuz.

data.title: Yemen's Houthis Say Saudi Arabia Launched 93 Attacks on Yemen in 24 Hours
data.description: On the evening of October 30, Yemen's Houthi movement said Saudi Arabia carried out 93 airstrikes and missile attacks on Yemen in the previous 24 hours, targeting Sana'a and the governorates of Al Jawf, Taiz, Saada, Marib, Dhamar, Hajjah, Ibb, and Lahij. According to Sina Finance, the Houthis said the cumulative number of Saudi airstrikes and missile attacks since the current escalation began had reached 3,689.

data.title: Yemen Government Forces Say Houthis Attacked Aden International Airport and Maashiq Palace
data.description: A Yemeni government military spokesperson said Houthi forces attacked Aden International Airport and Maashiq Palace with ballistic missiles on the evening of October 30 local time. According to Sina Finance, Maashiq Palace is the Yemeni president’s residence in the temporary capital of Aden and an office of the Yemeni government there.

data.title: Tom Curtis: Burger King Comparable-Sales Growth Reached 8.4%
data.description:
Burger King US and Canada President Tom Curtis said comparable sales growth was 8.4%, versus an estimate of 6.2%, Bloomberg reported. He said growth was driven largely by former customers returning after reconnecting with the brand.

Curtis discussed the sales turnaround with Romaine Bostick on “The Close.”

data.title: Illumina CEO: Q3 Beat Expectations, Q4 Outlook Raised; Growth Target Stands for 2027
data.description: Illumina CEO Jacob Thaysen said the company beat expectations in the third quarter and raised its fourth-quarter outlook, according to Bloomberg. He said Illumina has shifted from essentially flat performance to mid-single-digit growth over the past 18 months and remains committed to its high-single-digit growth target for 2027. Clinical business is the main growth driver. Thaysen spoke with Romaine Bostick on “The Close.”

data.title: U.S. Treasury Market: Safe-Haven Buying Lifts Short-Dated Notes as Federal Funds Futures Volume Surges
data.description:
U.S. Treasury prices rose in a bull steepening on Friday, with short- and intermediate-term notes outperforming as safe-haven demand supported the market amid a selloff in large-cap technology stocks.

According to Sina Finance, shortly after 3 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time, front- and intermediate-term yields were down about 2 basis points, while the 2s10s and 5s30s spreads widened 1.5 and 3 basis points, respectively. Near the close, month-end duration-extension flows sharply narrowed swap spreads. The Nasdaq 100 was poised to enter its third technical correction of the year after falling about 10% from its peak amid disappointing technology earnings. Treasury futures volume was about 20% above its 20-day average by 3 p.m., and November federal funds futures volume approached 500,000 contracts late in the session amid heavy buying at 96.120.

At 4:47 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time, the 2-year Treasury yield was down 1 basis point at 4.5876%, the 5-year yield fell 2.1 basis points to 4.7215%, the 10-year yield declined 0.6 basis point to 4.931%, and the 30-year yield rose 1 basis point to 5.3093%. The 5s30s spread widened about 2.9 basis points to 58.42 basis points, while the 2s10s spread widened about 0.4 basis point to 33.93 basis points. The 10-year yield closed down about 1 basis point at 4.93%, near the lower end of its 4.89%-5.05% range for the week.

data.title: MS NOW: U.S. President Donald Trump's Administration Prepared for Short, Intense Airstrikes as Early as November 4
data.description: According to Jin10, MS NOW reported, citing three senior Gulf officials, that U.S. President Donald Trump's administration had informed its Gulf allies it was prepared to launch short, intense airstrikes as early as November 4, the day after the midterm elections.

data.title: Binance News Update | Binance Co-CEOs Say 80% of the $6.3 Billion Loss Is Already Covered, With Withdrawals Restarting in Phases and Proof of Reserves Due Monday
data.description: Binance co-CEOs Yi He and Richard Teng said the exchange has already covered about 80% of the roughly $6.3 billion lost in its security incident and will absorb the full cost itself. In a letter to users dated Friday, October 30, they said Binance’s hot wallets were compromised at about 20:05 UTC on October 29.“Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users,” they wrote.About 80% Already CoveredBinance will cover all stolen funds through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and its corporate treasury, the co-CEOs said. The exchange has set aside more than $6.34 billion, $5 billion of which is held in the exact tokens that were stolen, including USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH and BNB. That covers about 80% of the loss, and Binance is buying the remaining tokens through market and over-the-counter channels.What Binance Has Done So FarSince identifying the incident, Binance has:Contained the compromised infrastructure, revoked affected authorizations and added controls to prevent further unauthorized activity.Frozen about $3 billion on-chain with help from law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, asset issuers and industry partners.Strengthened security checks across affected systems.Paused withdrawals for security reviews, while keeping deposits and other unaffected services running.What the Investigation Has FoundBinance’s initial investigation pointed to a compromised laptop, and further work has uncovered additional points of breach. The exchange said it has found no evidence that wallet private keys were leaked. It is working with internal and external security experts to map the full attack sequence and expects to share further verified technical findings in about 48 hours.Withdrawals and Proof of ReservesBinance said in Friday’s letter that it aimed to start resuming withdrawals within about 34 hours, in phases, once security checks are complete. It also planned an initial Proof of Reserves snapshot within 12 hours, with results by Monday, November 2, so users can verify their balances and how they are backed.The exchange will also publish a post-mortem report covering what happened, lessons learned and new safeguards. “We take full responsibility for addressing this security incident, strengthening our security infrastructure, and ensuring our users are protected,” the co-CEOs wrote.

data.title: Google and Pentagon Discuss Cooperation on Golden Dome Project
data.description: Google and the Pentagon are reportedly discussing cooperation on the Golden Dome project. According to ChainCatcher, market sources reported the talks.

data.title: STOCKS | Earnings-Season Selloffs Intensify for Companies Missing Estimates
data.description: U.S. stocks are seeing some of the harshest post-earnings selloffs on record for companies that miss expectations, as investors grow more sensitive to slowing profit growth. According to Sina Finance, Amazon plunged on Friday after its earnings report, while Alphabet fell by a record amount on Thursday following disappointing results; selloffs in communication services stocks that miss estimates have been the steepest since data collection began in 2019, with a similar pattern in heavyweight technology stocks. With earnings season about one-third complete, S&P 500 companies’ earnings growth has slowed to about 26%, from 32% in the second quarter. Strategists at Wells Fargo and Franklin Templeton have warned in recent weeks that higher interest rates, trade-tariff pressures, and elevated oil prices could slow earnings growth. Industry research data cited in the report put third-quarter technology earnings growth at 65%, down from nearly 77% in the prior quarter, and communication services growth at 3.2%, down from nearly 10%. Technology and communication services were the only sectors to fall this month, while all other sectors rose. Northlight Asset Management Chief Investment Officer Chris Zaccarelli said the market is more sensitive than usual and investors would rather sell first than risk further losses. Truist Advisory Services Chief Investment Officer and Chief Market Strategist Keith Lerner said the two sectors make up half the market, leading investors to demand more evidence that the trade remains viable; he added that slower growth challenges that narrative. Bokeh Capital Partners Chief Investment Officer Kimberly Forrest said investors are trimming some of technology stocks’ prior excess gains and buying cheaper stocks in other areas rather than leaving the market entirely. Overall earnings are still expected to grow: industry research estimates put S&P 500 earnings growth closer to 20% during 2027 and into the first quarter of 2028. Franklin Templeton Institute Chief Investment Strategist Jeff Schulze said that would exceed the historical 10% threshold associated with further market gains after earnings growth peaks, and that the S&P 500 could return high single digits to low double digits in 2027 if earnings meet expectations. So far, the share of S&P 500 companies beating Wall Street estimates is at its lowest level this year, including in technology, consumer discretionary, and financials. Zaccarelli said earnings misses in one area could prompt rapid repricing across related areas.

data.title: Fitch: France's Rating Supported by GDP per Capita and Strong Governance Indicators
data.description: According to Jin10, Fitch said France's rating is supported by several factors, including GDP per capita above the median for the 'A' rating category and governance indicators far above the median for its rating category.
